properties.description: Loads a RANGE of months by generating the (year, month) pairs between startYearMonth and endYearMonth and calling PL_Master_NycTaxi_Load for each. This is how you populate a brand-new environment: trigger it once with 202401 -> 202412 and walk away. isSequential is TRUE by design; see the comment on the ForEach activity.

activities.name: Calculate Month Count
activities.description: Number of months in the inclusive range. YYYYMM is not a linear number - 202412 to 202501 is a difference of 89, not 1 - so convert to an absolute month ordinal (year*12 + month) before subtracting.

activities.name: Validate Range

message.value: @concat('Backfill range ', string(pipeline().parameters.startYearMonth), ' to ', string(pipeline().parameters.endYearMonth), ' resolves to ', string(variables('monthCount')), ' months. Expected between 1 and 120. Check that both parameters are YYYYMM and that start <= end.')

activities.description: Fails the run on an invalid range. The loop is NOT nested inside this IfCondition: ADF rejects a container activity inside another container activity, and both IfCondition and ForEach are containers. The pipeline validated and deployed happily and then failed at RUN time with "Operation on target Validate Range failed: Container activity cannot include another container activity". Guarding here and depending on success below is equivalent - an invalid range fails this activity, so For Each Month never runs - and it is legal.

activities.name: For Each Month
activities.description: isSequential = true, deliberately. The three stages contend for the same resources - the same managed-VNet IR, the same serverless pool, the same staging table (which PL_Load_Sql_YellowTrip truncates). Running months in parallel would corrupt the staging load. If you need a faster backfill, raise dataIntegrationUnits on the copy activities rather than parallelising here.

activities.name: Load One Month
activities.description: Converts the zero-based offset back into a (year, month) pair via an absolute month ordinal. The `sub(..., 1)` / `add(..., 1)` dance converts between 1-12 months and 0-11 arithmetic so that December does not become month 0 of the following year.
